meta.title: AI Design Toolkit for Creative Teams | Vibhor Mathur
meta.description: How a creative director's studio builds its own AI tools: automating set tasks, scaling production and shipping interactive web campaigns without a developer.

label: AI Toolkit
headline: Tools that make the *work*, built by the people who make the work.
intro: AI is not only a way to make images. Used properly, it lets a design team build its own software: tools for the studio, tools for marketing, and interactive web experiences that designers ship themselves. This is that toolkit, and what it changed.

principles.title: Prompts are inputs
principles.body: A prompt is one ingredient, not the product. The product is what you wrap around it.

principles.title: Tools are modules
principles.body: Small tools with a single job, each with a proper interface, that can be combined and reused.

principles.title: Systems create consistency
principles.body: Brand, lighting, faces and scenes are held in the tool, so the hundredth output looks like the first.

pillars.title: Automate the set tasks
pillars.body: Work that repeats, such as turning one founder photo into a campaign library or one product shot into a scene, stops being a design request and becomes a button. The designers' time goes to the idea and the finish.

proof.label: Founder Image Generator
proof.detail: One photo in, a full campaign library out. 4K, one click.

proof.label: Social Content Gen
proof.detail: A founder photo and a business story in, a composed, campaign-ready post out.

pillars.title: Scale up production
pillars.body: When the tool holds the look, volume stops costing quality. The same pipeline that produced 81 television films for 20 founders also produced a newspaper front page and more than 200 social posts, with no cameras, sets or lights.

proof.label: Razorbae, AI avatar
proof.detail: Shot once, trained into a system: 129 reels and 6.55 million views.

pillars.title: Easy to learn, even for beginners
pillars.body: A blank prompt box is intimidating. A panel with lenses, lighting, presets and references is not. Wrapping models in clear interfaces gives a beginner a good starting point on day one, and gives the whole team one shared way of working.

proof.label: Interfaces, not prompts
proof.detail: Every tool is built with an interface in Gemini Studio, so the controls are visible and the learning curve is short.

proof.label: Workshops and mentoring
proof.detail: AI design workshops, talks and one-to-one mentoring for designers starting out.

pillars.title: Designers shipping interactive web, themselves
pillars.body: Campaign sites, landing pages and playable games used to wait in a developer queue. With AI-assisted building, designers take an idea from sketch to a live interactive page, and own the motion, the feel and the details end to end.

proof.label: Magic Checkout landing page
proof.detail: An immersive scroll-through world with micro-animations.

proof.label: Back in the Ring
proof.detail: A parallax landing page and a playable game.

tools_head.label: The studio's tools
tools_head.title: Built in-house. Used on live campaigns.
tools_head.body: Each one started as a repeating task on a real campaign, and became a tool the whole team could pick up.

tools.name: Cinematography Tool
tools.body: A virtual camera department. Pick the lens, set the light, choose the grade, and the scene follows.
tools.built_with: Gemini Studio for the interface, Nano Banana API

tools.name: Product Image Generator
tools.body: Virtual product photography that keeps the brand together. Drop in a product and get it placed in an environment, lit and composed.
tools.built_with: Gemini Studio for the interface, Nano Banana API

tools.name: Advanced Image Editor
tools.body: One scene, many angles, the same faces. Built for the moments where a single hero image is not enough and consistency is the whole job.
bullets: A consistent scene from different angles
Multi-reference generation: scene, style, lighting, colour and face
tools.built_with: Gemini Studio for the interface, Nano Banana API

tools.name: Founder Image Generator
tools.body: Converts one founder image into multiple visuals across clothing, pose and lighting. It was the engine behind the T20 campaign.
bullets: Transformations across clothing, pose and lighting
20+ founders from a single source photo each

tools.name: Social Content Gen
tools.body: A high-volume, personalised post creator. Give it a founder image and a business success story; preset combinations of clothing, pose, lighting and background do the rest.
bullets: Input: a founder image and a business story
Preset clothing, pose, lighting and background
tools.built_with: Replit, Gemini, ChatGPT and Nano Banana

interactive.label: Interactive web
interactive.title: Pages you can play with, shipped by designers.
interactive.body: Beyond images and films, the team has had interactive web experiences built for campaigns: landing pages with scroll worlds, micro-animations and a playable game. They sit alongside the toolkit because they use the same idea: design owns the idea and the feel, and AI shortens the distance to something live.

items.title: Magic Checkout
items.body: An immersive landing page where you experience what checkout does, from the magic you see to the science behind it.

items.title: Back in the Ring
items.body: A parallax landing page that pulls you into the ring, plus a game where each opponent defeated unlocks a new feature.

items.title: The Wall of Laughter
items.body: An anonymous digital board where HR professionals shared the funniest salary questions they had ever received.

items.title: Backing India's Boldest
items.body: Glambot-style camera motion videos of founders for a landing page and social content, built around character realism and cinematic slow motion.

learn.label: Learning
learn.title: The tools are only half of it. The team has to be able to use them.
learn.body: Beginners are the point. The toolkit is taught, not just handed over: through workshops, talks and mentoring that start from what AI can do for a designer.
